title: CFG++ samplers, and why cfg is near 1 there
hook: One swap inside the sampler: re-noise with the unconditional prediction. That moves cfg to a different scale, and it means cfg 1 still costs two predictions.

verified.claim: euler_cfg_pp computes the next sample from the guided denoised value and the unconditional prediction's noise.
The sampler sets disable_cfg1_optimization, so cfg 1 still runs both predictions.
The lab's port equals the real sample_euler_cfg_pp, using a stand-in model, at cfg 0.6, 1 and 1.5.
verified.ref: Our comparison on a CPU, v0.43.0

verified.claim: The paper's lambda runs from 0 to 1, and its table pairs lambda 0.6 with cfg 7.5 and lambda 1.0 with cfg 12.5 at 50 steps, matched by LPIPS.
Our render used euler_cfg_pp at cfg 1, normal schedule, 20 steps, on SDXL.

unchecked: One render, one seed. We have no CFG++ render at another cfg, so no picture here shows it overshooting.
The toy's mapping to plain cfg differs from the paper's, as expected for a toy. Don't use either as an exact conversion.
We read the Euler CFG++ code closely. We read the other CFG++ samplers only far enough to see them use the same flag, and did not port them.
